mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates on future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% over a 3-month window signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting central bank hawkishness and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in low-unemployment regimes is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction starts above 1.2 million units per month signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives higher corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds 1.2 million, or the average 60-day return in high-housing-start regimes is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market contraction, indicating an impending economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above $385 billion signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS exceeds $385 billion, or the average 5-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL above 210.5 over a 3-month window signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or increase interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 210.5, or the average return in high-inflation periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market recovery, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized over a quarter signals strong aggregate demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the average 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
